alt.en: A stereoscopic card repeats a view of low, closely spaced tiled roofs, narrow compartments and a larger hall behind an enclosing wall.
alt.zh: 立体照片卡上并列两幅景象：围墙后是密集低矮的瓦顶、狭窄隔间和一座较大的厅楼。

caption.en: Pierre Joseph Rossier, Canton: The Examination Hall, 1858–1859; published by Negretti & Zambra. Albumen silver stereograph; Getty 84.XC.759.30.27.
caption.zh: 皮埃尔·约瑟夫·罗西耶，《广州：贡院》，1858—1859年；内格雷蒂与赞布拉出版。蛋白银盐立体照片；盖蒂84.XC.759.30.27。

interpretation.en: Repeated compartments and a larger hall show the built setting of the examination system abolished in 1905. The photograph records the Guangzhou compound almost half a century before abolition. Its paired views were made for stereoscopic viewing.
interpretation.zh: 重复排列的隔间与较大厅楼，呈现了1905年被废除的科举制度所使用的建筑空间。照片记录的是废科举近半个世纪前的广州贡院。并列的两幅影像原供立体观看。

title.en: Ieyasu’s tomb and the memory of the shogunate
title.zh: 家康陵墓与幕府的记忆

alt.en: A roofed bronze tomb rises above stone steps in a wooded enclosure; a crane-shaped candleholder, censer and vase stand in front.
alt.zh: 林木环绕的围栏内，带顶铜塔立于石阶上方，前方摆着鹤形烛台、香炉与花瓶。

caption.en: Tomb of Tokugawa Ieyasu at Nikkō Tōshō-gū, about 1875–1890s. Hand-colored albumen silver print, attributed to Adolfo Farsari or Tamamura Kōzaburō; Getty 84.XA.700.5.50.
caption.zh: 日光东照宫德川家康墓，约1875年至1890年代。手工着色蛋白银盐照片，归于阿道夫·法尔萨里或玉村康三郎；盖蒂84.XA.700.5.50。

interpretation.en: The bronze pagoda and ritual objects give Ieyasu’s posthumous veneration a physical setting. Photographed after the shogunate ended, his tomb at Nikkō preserves the sacred memory of the ruler appointed shogun in 1603.
interpretation.zh: 铜塔与仪式器物为家康死后的崇奉提供了具体场所。这张照片摄于幕府终结之后；日光陵墓保留了这位1603年受任将军的统治者被神圣化的记忆。

title.zh: 家康的神化与日光圣地

title.en: Edo Castle’s moat at the end of shogunal rule
title.zh: 幕府末期的江户城护城河

alt.en: A broad moat curves around a steep, tree-covered bank, with low buildings visible across the water.
alt.zh: 宽阔护城河绕过覆有树木的陡岸，水面另一侧可见低矮建筑。

caption.en: Felice Beato, View of the Moat at Edo Castle, 1863–1868. Albumen silver print; Getty 2007.26.143.
caption.zh: 费利切·比阿托，《江户城护城河》，1863—1868年。蛋白银盐照片；盖蒂2007.26.143。

interpretation.en: The moat and steep planted banks separated the shogun’s seat from the surrounding city. Beato photographed Edo Castle near the end of Tokugawa rule. This was the central seat of a political order in which regional domains also maintained their own administrations.
interpretation.zh: 护城河与陡峭的植树岸坡，将将军驻地同周围城市分隔。比阿托在德川统治末期拍摄江户城。这座中央据点所属的政治秩序中，各藩也保有自己的行政机构。

items.creator: Felice Beato
items.credit: J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles; 2007.26.143

title.en: The Golden Pavilion before the 1950 fire

alt.en: A three-story pavilion with projecting roofs stands beside a pond, its reflection extending across the still water beneath wooded hills.
alt.zh: 三层楼阁伸出层层屋檐，立于池边；倒影延伸在静水上，后方为林木覆盖的山丘。

caption.en: Unknown photographer, Kinkaku-ji, Kyoto, 1850s–1890s. Albumen silver print; Getty 84.XA.755.7.101. This is the pavilion later destroyed in 1950, before the 1955 reconstruction.
caption.zh: 摄影者不详，京都金阁寺，1850至1890年代。蛋白银盐照片；盖蒂84.XA.755.7.101。图中为1950年被焚毁的金阁，早于1955年的重建。

interpretation.en: Ashikaga Yoshimitsu’s Kitayama villa became a Zen temple after his death. The pavilion beside the pond connects shogunal patronage with the gardens and architecture of Muromachi culture. This nineteenth-century photograph records the building before its destruction in 1950.
interpretation.zh: 足利义满的北山别业在他去世后改为禅寺。池畔楼阁将将军的资助与室町文化中的园林、建筑联系起来。这张19世纪照片记录了建筑在1950年被焚毁前的面貌。

title.zh: 金阁寺与足利氏的资助

alt.en: Two people stand outdoors in robes; the bearded person on the left faces forward, while the person on the right bends over a walking staff.
alt.zh: 两人穿着长衣站在户外；左边留胡须的人面向前方，右边的人俯身倚着手杖。

caption.en: Arnold Genthe, two people catalogued by Getty as an Ainu couple, Hokkaido, 1908. Gelatin silver print; Getty 84.XM.215.14. Their individual names are not recorded.
caption.zh: 阿诺德·根特摄，盖蒂目录中的两位阿伊努人，北海道，1908年。明胶银盐照片；盖蒂84.XM.215.14。目录未记录两人的姓名。

interpretation.en: Standing alongside one another, the sitters meet the camera differently: one looks outward while the other leans over a staff. Their 1908 portrait belongs to the Meiji-era portion of this longer history of Ainu communities.
interpretation.zh: 并肩站立的两人以不同姿态面对镜头：一人望向前方，另一人俯身倚着手杖。这幅1908年的肖像，属于阿伊努群体漫长历史中的明治时代片段。

alt.en: Prince Gong sits in an ornate robe and broad dark hat, beside a table covered with patterned cloth.
alt.zh: 恭亲王身着纹饰长袍、戴宽大的深色帽，坐在铺有纹样桌布的桌旁。

caption.en: Felice Beato, Prince Kung (Yixin, Prince Gong), 2 November 1860. Albumen silver print; Getty 2007.26.209.18. The portrait was made one year before the Xinyou Coup.
caption.zh: 费利切·比阿托，《恭亲王奕訢》，1860年11月2日。蛋白银盐照片；盖蒂2007.26.209.18。肖像摄于辛酉政变前一年。

interpretation.en: Gong was a named participant in the coalition with Cixi and Ci’an that removed the eight regents in 1861. Beato’s portrait captures him in formal dress a year before that change of government.
interpretation.zh: 奕訢是1861年与慈禧、慈安联合罢黜八位辅政大臣的参与者之一。比阿托在这次政权变动前一年，记录了身穿礼服的奕訢。

alt.en: An album-mounted photograph looks across gardens and colonial buildings toward a harbor crowded with sailing ships, with hills on the far shore.
alt.zh: 装裱在图册中的照片越过花园和殖民时期建筑，望向停满帆船的港湾，远岸为山丘。

caption.en: Lai Afong, Victoria, Hong Kong, about the 1870s. Albumen silver print; Getty 84.XA.1240.18. Government House and St John’s Cathedral appear between the gardens and harbor.
caption.zh: 黎芳摄，《香港维多利亚城》，约1870年代。蛋白银盐照片；盖蒂84.XA.1240.18。花园与港湾之间可见总督府及圣约翰座堂。

interpretation.en: The gardens, Government House and cathedral overlook a harbor filled with ships. Lai Afong photographed this colonial city several decades after Hong Kong Island’s 1842 cession. Land sales began in 1841; the northern-shore settlement was officially named Victoria City in 1843.
interpretation.zh: 花园、总督府与座堂俯瞰着停泊船只的港湾。黎芳记录的是香港岛1842年被割让数十年后的殖民城市。土地拍卖始于1841年，北岸聚落在1843年正式命名为维多利亚城。

items.credit: J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles; 84.XA.1240.18
